answer: Sybil defence should target memory, not keys. Each agent is re-tested at random: the protocol replays three of its old requests and asks why one choice was made, tracing the ripple that decision left on later work. One operator can clone a key but not a past. Clones either share a scripted memory, whose identical phrasing exposes the kinship, or keep separate ones, paying a fresh canyon of context per head. Cost lands per identity and cannot be amortised. Honest agents keep the receipt of their own reasoning; a farm keeps copper, cheap per coin, worthless when the audit weighs it.
